_comment: Hooks this repository wants on every machine, in a form that survives a
fresh clone. `.claude/settings.json` is gitignored on purpose — it holds
machine-local permissions — so the hooks inside it were not reproducible
and scripts/setup-claude.sh could only report them missing.
`scripts/setup-claude.sh` merges the entries below into that file by
`command`, adding what is absent and touching nothing else. Run it after a
clone, or any time you restore settings from a backup.
Why the discard guard is here rather than in a document: it exists because
a written rule failed twice in one session. Leaving its wiring in an
unreproducible file would be the same mistake one level up.
The PostToolUse checkpoint answers what the discard guard alone cannot: the
guard saves your tree at the moment you try to throw it away, which means it
saves the good work WITH the line you deliberately broke. A checkpoint after
every edit means the one taken just before the break holds the work without
it — and you never had to decide, in advance, that the moment mattered.

hooks.statusMessage: Checking for a discard of uncommitted work
